फर्जी सहमति पत्र जमा किए जाने के आरोपों से संबंधित थी. अधिवक्ता संगम गर्ग के जरिए भेजे गए नोटिस में कहा गया है कि कई सामग्रियों में घुम्मन पर यह आरोप लगाया गया कि वह पंजाब सरकार के भीतर एक कथित ‘ट्रांसफर-पोस्टिंग नेटवर्क’, ‘नेक्सस’ या ‘रैकेट’ को “नियंत्रित, संचालित, सुविधाजनक बनाते या उससे लाभान्वित” होते हैं और भ्रष्ट गतिविधियों में शामिल हैं. नोटिस पाने वालों में हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स , द प्रिंट , एबीपी सांझा और पीटीसी न्यूज के अलावा गूगल, मेटा और एक्स भी शामिल हैं. नोटिस में इन खबरों और सामग्री को “झूठा, निराधार, लापरवाह, प्रेरित और दुर्भावनापूर्ण” बताया गया है. इसमें आरोप लगाया गया है कि सामग्री प्रकाशित करने से पहले घुम्मन या किसी सक्षम आधिकारिक स्रोत से आरोपों की पुष्टि के लिए “कोई निष्पक्ष या सार्थक प्रयास” नहीं किया गया. नोटिस में कथित मानहानिकारक सामग्री को वापस लेने की मांग के साथ इसे आईटी नियम, 2021 के तहत औपचारिक शिकायत और शिकायत-निवारण प्रक्रिया के तौर पर भी पेश किया गया है. साथ ही सभी नोटिस प्राप्तकर्ताओं से संबंधित इलेक्ट्रॉनिक और भौतिक साक्ष्यों को सुरक्षित रखने को कहा गया है. नोटिस में चेतावनी दी गई है कि तय समयसीमा के भीतर अनुपालन न करने, इनकार करने, टालमटोल करने या अधूरे अनुपालन की स्थिति में घुम्मन के पास संबंधित पक्षों के खिलाफ बिना किसी और पत्राचार के सभी उचित दीवानी, आपराधिक, वैधानिक और नियामकीय कार्रवाई शुरू करने के अलावा कोई विकल्प नहीं बचेगा. इससे पहले घुम्मन ने इसी तरह के आरोपों को लेकर शिरोमणि अकाली दल के नेता बिक्रम सिंह मजीठिया को भी कानूनी नोटिस भेजा था. क्या मीडिया सत्ता या कॉर्पोरेट हितों के बजाय जनता के हित में काम कर सकता है? बिल्कुल कर सकता है, लेकिन तभी जब वह धन के लिए सत्ता या कॉरपोरेट स्रोतों के बजाय जनता पर निर्भर हो. इसका अर्थ है कि आपको खड़े होना पड़ेगा और खबरों को आज़ाद रखने के लिए थोड़ा खर्च करना होगा. सब्सक्राइब करें. जसवंत खालड़ा और पंजाब की दहशतगर्दी

items.title: Bhagwant Mann’s OSD sends notice to media outlets over ‘baseless’ reports on ‘nexus’
items.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s officer on special duty, Rajbir Singh Ghuman, has sent a notice to several media platforms and tech intermediaries to take down alleged defamatory content against him. The matter pertains to reports about the Enforcement Directorate’s purported letter to the Punjab DGP that alleged Rajbir Singh Ghuman was involved in influencing transfers and postings of government officials, leaking confidential government documents, facilitating arms licences and securing government approvals in lieu of alleged monetary and other benefits. According to reports, the said letter stemmed from a money laundering investigation linked to the submission of alleged fake consent letters for obtaining change of land use in a case involving a housing society. The notice, filed through advocate Sangam Garg, said that a series of material alleged that Ghuman “controls, operates, facilitates, or benefits from a corrupt ‘transfer-posting network’, ‘nexus’, or ‘racket’ within the government of Punjab and is complicit in corrupt practices”. Among the outlets named in the notice are Hindustan Times , The Print , ABP Sanjha , and PTC News , apart from Google, Meta and X. The notice terms the news reports as “false, baseless, reckless, motivated and malicious” and says that “no fair or meaningful attempt” was made to verify the allegations from Ghuman or with any competent official source. Apart from retraction of the said defamatory content, the notice said it constituted a formal complaint and grievance under the IT Rules 2021. It also called on all the noticees to preserve all relevant electronic and physical evidence relating to the impugned content. The notice states that “failure, refusal, evasion or incomplete compliance within the applicable period shall leave my client with no alternative but to initiate, without further correspondence, all appropriate civil, criminal, statutory and regulatory proceedings against the defaultee noticee or notices”. items.title: Who will lead India’s next student movement?
items.summary: In this episode of What's Your ISM?, TNM Executive Editor Sudipto Mondal sits down with student leaders from the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and Ambedkar Students’ Association (ASA) to discuss the new opportunities to build student politics, the growing anger on Indian campuses, and the possibilities and contradictions within today’s student movements. Sudipto and the student leaders also explore the relationship between caste and class politics, Ambedkar and Marx, the Left and Ambedkarite movements, and whether these forces can find common ground. They discuss the recent student protests, the rise of Gen Z politics, the education crisis, privatisation, unemployment, and the demand for student union elections in Karnataka. The conversation also looks at whether student organisations can build a third front beyond the BJP and Congress, the challenges of organising across caste and class lines, and the role of ideology in sustaining a movement beyond a single protest. They also discuss the Rohith Act campaign in Karnataka, and how different student organisations came together to push for stronger protections against discrimination in universities. items.title: 9 घंटे की आनाकानी के बाद पुलिस ने दर्ज की अजीत भारती के खिलाफ एफआईआर
items.summary: दिल्ली के नॉर्थ एवेन्यू थाने में यूट्यूबर अजीत भारती के खिलाफ एससीएसटी एक्ट, आईटी एक्ट और बीएनएस की गंभीर धाराओं में एफआईआर दर्ज की गई है. भारती ने अपने यूट्यूब पर एक वीडियो में डॉ. आंबेडकर, नगीना से सांसद चंद्रशेखर आज़ाद और दलित समाज के बारे में टिप्पणियां की थी. साथ ही उन्होंने दलित समाज की महिलाओं को लेकर बेहद आपत्तिजनक यौन टिप्पणियां भी की. इसके बाद आजाद समाज पार्टी के कार्यकर्ताओं ने 23 अगस्त रविवार की देर शाम थाने में लंबी जद्दोजहद के बाद एफआईआर दर्ज कराई है. मामले में शिकायतकर्ता और आजाद समाज पार्टी के दिल्ली प्रदेश अध्यक्ष बालकराम बौद्ध के मुताबिक, भारती ने अपने यूट्यूब पर 'आरक्षण हटाओ नौटंकी' और जंतर-मंतर पर हुए प्रदर्शनों के मुद्दे पर चर्चा करते हुए आपत्तिजनक टिप्पणियां कीं. भारती ने इस वीडियो में जातिसूचक शब्दों के साथ-साथ चंद्रशेखर की शक्ल और उनकी मूंछों पर थूकने की भी बात कही है. हालांकि, अजीत भारती के यूट्यूब चैनल पर अब यह वीडियो उपलब्ध नहीं है. इस एफआईआर में तीन अलग-अलग कानूनों की कुल 9 धाराएं लगाई गई हैं. इसमें अनुसूचित जाति एवं अनुसूचित जनजाति (अत्याचार निवारण) अधिनियम, 1989 की धारा 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(1)(u), 3(1)(v), 3(1)(w)(ii) और 3(2)(va) के तहत मुकदमा दर्ज किया गया है. इसके अलावा दूसरा भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023 की धारा 196 (1)(c) और 351(3) लगाई गई है. साथ ही सूचना एवं प्रौद्योगिकी अधिनियम, 2000 की धारा 67 के तहत मुकदमा दर्ज किया गया है. शिकायतकर्ता की मांग है कि आरोपी के खिलाफ सख्त कानूनी कार्रवाई की जाए और संबंधित सोशल मीडिया अकाउंट्स से इस वीडियो को हटवाया जाए. वहीं, इस एफआईआर के बाद अजीत भारती ने एक्स पर लिखा , "मैं जानता हूं कि दिल्ली पुलिस के नॉर्थ एवेन्यू में आजाद समाज पार्टी वालों ने कितना दवाब दे कर रात के बारह बजे यह एफआईआर लिखवाई है, जो कोर्ट में दो मिनट नहीं टिकेगी. एक भी धारा ऐसी नहीं है, जो होल्ड करेगी…. यदि ऐसा कमेंट फिर मेरे वीडियो पर आया तो मैं पुनः उसी तरीके से उत्तर दूंगा जो मैंने दिया." बता दें कि जंतर-मंतर पर 21 अगस्त को ‘आरक्षण हटाओ आंदोलन’ (आरएचए) के बैनर/सोशल मीडिया अभियान के तहत बुलाया गया था. यहां प्रदर्शनकारियों ने जाति आधारित आरक्षण और यूजीसी के इक्विटी नियमों का विरोध किया था. इसी सिलसिले में अजीत भारती भी जंतर-मंतर पहुंचे थे. जहां उन्होंने लोगों को संबोधित भी किया. इसके बाद उन्होंने वहां आए लोगों का धन्यवाद करते हुए अपने यूट्यूब चैनल पर लाइव किया. लाइव के दौरान वह कमेंट पढ़कर उनका जवाब दे रहे थे. इसी लाइव बातबीत के दौरान किसी ने कमेंट किया कि अजीत भाई अपनी बहन की शादी एमपी चंद्रशेखर से कर दो, रिजर्वेशन खत्म हो जाएगा. इसी का जवाब देते हुए अजीत अपना आपा खो बैठे और उन्होंने पूरे दलित समाज को घेर लिया और आपत्तिजनक एवं अश्लील टिप्पणी की. इस पूरे मामले पर आजाद समाज पाटी के दिल्ली प्रदेश प्रभारी महेश पहवाल न्यूज़ल

items.title: A year after Israeli strikes killed journalists at a hospital, no one has been held accountable
items.summary: It’s been a year since Israeli soldiers killed 22 Palestinians , including journalists and rescue workers, in a double strike on a hospital in Gaza. No one has been held accountable. Israeli officials said the target was a suspected Hamas camera on the roof of Nasser Hospital. Among those killed were Reuters cameraman Hussam al-Masri and Mariam Dagga , a visual journalist who worked for The Associated Press and other news organisations. Despite repeated requests by AP , the army hasn’t provided details about the investigation or a timeline for when it could be completed. Rights groups say Israel rarely holds troops accountable for killing Palestinians, pointing to long investigations that rarely lead to prosecution . As global outrage over the August 25, 2025, strikes grew, the Israeli military said that in addition to taking out the camera, six of those killed were linked to Hamas, without providing evidence. But an Israeli soldier, speaking on condition of anonymity for fear of retribution, now says the military could find no evidence linking the camera, which belonged to al-Masri, to Hamas. The soldier, who was privy to discussions surrounding the military’s response, said none of the six was the intended target of the strikes. AP sent detailed questions to the military about the allegations, as well as other questions about the strikes. The military didn’t address the questions but said the incident is being examined and findings will be transferred to the Military Advocate General’s Corps to reach a verdict on whether to open a criminal investigation. It didn’t provide a timeline. AP reported at the time that one of the six Israel said was linked to Hamas wasn’t on the hospital’s list of casualties and two others were medical or emergency personnel. That, along with the soldier’s account, raises serious questions about Israel’s rationale for the strikes. Why did troops fail to identify the cameraman as al-Masri, even though journalists were known to film at the hospital? Why did they strike a second time, causing most of the deaths and raising accusations of a “double tap” attack on first responders, which would be a war crime? AP and Reuters released a statement Tuesday calling again for Israel to provide a full explanation of the strikes. items.title: Supreme Court orders States to set up SITs to probe fraudulent motor accident insurance claims
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently directed all States to constitute dedicated Special Investigation Teams (SITs) to investigate suspected fraudulent motor accident insurance claims [ The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Tuni Pati & Ors. ]. By way of an order passed on August 17, a bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and PB Varale also directed insurance companies to refer all claims indicating fraud to the respective State SITs. The Court warned that the top management of insurance companies would be held accountable if cases are selectively referred. Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah Justice PB Varale The proceedings before the top court started with a dispute over whether a vehicle shown as being involved in an accident was actually the vehicle involved. However, the case revealed a larger pattern in which the same vehicle was allegedly shown as being involved in multiple accidents to facilitate fraudulent claims. The Court said the apparent fraud was of an “enormous proportion” and that it had therefore expanded the scope of the proceedings to examine and check such claims. The Bench noted that fraudulent claims not only put financial pressure on insurance companies but could also affect genuine consumers through higher premiums. Thus, it directed every State to set up a dedicated SIT and forward all complaints received from insurance companies to the body for expeditious investigation. States have also been asked to provide sufficient personnel to the SITs and disclose the procedure adopted for investigating such complaints. The Court further made insurance companies responsible for ensuring that all claims indicative of fraud are referred to the SITs. It warned that the top management of an insurance company would be held accountable if the Court found that suspicious claims had been selectively referred for investigation. The Court also directed insurers to initiate appropriate departmental action against their officials if a State SIT recommends action against them or an FIR is registered against them. The directions came after the Court was informed about steps already taken in Uttar Pradesh. The State told the Bench that a special SIT had been constituted to verify suspected fraudulent claims. items.title: Delhi High Court gives slum dwellers near PM Modi's residence 6 weeks to move to DUSIB colony
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday directed the residents of three slum clusters near Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence in the Race Course area to vacate within 6 weeks and move to the alternative location provided by government authorities. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that after 6 weeks, the government can clear the land with the help of the police. "The appellants shall vacate the dwelling in the three jhuggi jhopris within six weeks from today. And within this period, they shall be provided with the accommodations allotted to them in DUSIB Colony. Whereafter, they shall be evicted to clear the land, if necessary, with the assistance of the police," the Court ordered. It ruled that there had been no violation of the rehabilitation policy in moving the residents in this case. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia However, the Division Bench said that the government will be bound by its undertakings and the Court's previous orders requiring availability of amenities at DUSIB Colony . The Court has also constituted a committee under former Delhi judge Manmohan Sharma to monitor the rehabilitation of residents and to ensure that the amenities promised to them by the government are provided. The committee will also consist of members from various departments of the Delhi government and the Central government. It ordered the government to notify the constitution of this committee immediately. The Division Bench passed the order while dealing with appeals filed by residents of Bhai Ram Camp, DID Camp and Masjid Camp against a single judge's order upholding their eviction from these camps. The camps are located near the Race Course area and the residents are being relocated to a DUSIB Colony in Savda Ghevra, outer Delhi. Several residents of the 3 slums approached the High Court stating that shifting hundreds of families far from their current homes would disrupt livelihoods, education and access to healthcare. They said that many of them work as drivers, domestic workers and labourers in central Delhi and that relocation would place their jobs and schooling at risk. items.title: CJAR at DNLU announces two-day single credit course and international conference on new criminal laws
items.summary: The Centre for Criminal Justice Administration and Research (CJAR) at Dharmashastra National Law University (DNLU), Jabalpur, in collaboration with Agnel School of Law, Vashi, Navi Mumbai, has announced a two-day single credit course on new criminal laws. The course will be conducted between October 9 and 10, 2026, followed by an international conference on October 11. The course, which will be conducted in person at DNLU, is designed to provide an intensive and comprehensive exploration of the paradigm shift in India’s criminal justice system following the introduction of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The course seeks to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and the practical application of the new criminal laws. Registration will remain open until September 30. The conference, to be conducted in hybrid mode, is titled “Transforming Criminal Justice in India: Implementation of the New Criminal Laws, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Justice.” The conference comes against the backdrop of significant changes in India’s criminal justice framework and the increasing role of technology in policing, investigation, prosecution and adjudication. The conference will examine the implementation of the new criminal laws alongside emerging developments involving Artificial Intelligence, digital technologies, electronic evidence, forensic science and cybersecurity. The conference invites participation from academicians, advocates, legal professionals, research scholars and students and has also issued a call for original and unpublished research papers. Abstract submissions are open until 15 September 2026, with notification of acceptance scheduled for 18 September 2026. Full papers may be submitted until 2 October 2026, while registration for the conference will remain open until 30 September 2026. The three day academic programme is expected to provide a significant platform for examining the practical and legal implications of India’s new criminal laws while also exploring how emerging technologies are reshaping the administration of criminal justice. Please find the attached Boucher for complete details.

items.title: Plea before Supreme Court seeks stay on NALSA decision to discontinue LADCS contracts
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought responses from the Central government and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) on a plea challenging NALSA’s August 4 communication directing the discontinuation of contract renewals for lawyers engaged under the Legal Aid Defence Counsel System (LADCS). [Association of Legal Aid Defence Counsels v. UOI] A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale issued notice in the matter. The petition was filed by serving legal aid defence counsel and supporting staff engaged under the scheme in various districts of Assam, Meghalaya and Nagaland. The petitioners have sought a stay on the communication and continuation of the existing LADCS system until the case is decided. Justice M.M. Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B. Varale NALSA introduced the LADCS scheme in 2022 to provide legal assistance and representation in criminal cases along the lines of a public-defender system. The scheme came in the eye of the storm earlier this year after lawyers, particularly in Punjab, went on a strike last month, alleging that the scheme created a parallel State-funded criminal defence system which was affecting the practice of independent advocates. The strike was eventually called off on July 31 after various meetings were held between the bar bodies and High Court judges. Subsequently, NALSA announced the decision to discontinue contracts of lawyers engaged under the scheme. By way of a communication issued on August 4 this year, NALSA said that the contracts of legal aid defence counsel in Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh will not be renewed from September 2026 onwards. In the remaining States and Union Territories, their contracts will not be renewed once their existing contractual tenures expire. NALSA also directed that legal-aid cases be assigned to members of the bar, preferably young lawyers. According to the plea before the top court, NALSA’s decision would place the existing LADCS mechanism in suspended animation, even though a high-level committee constituted by NALSA in March 2026 to review the scheme is yet to submit its report. TNHRC ]. A Bench of Justices M Dhandapani and N Dilip Kumar , therefore, set aside a Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) order directing the payment of compensation to a passenger who alleged that a bus conductor had behaved rudely with him before forcing him to de-board a bus. Justice M Dhandapani and Justice N Dilip Kumar The Court was hearing a petition filed by S Chidambara Selvan, an employee of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation. He challenged an SHRC order passed in September 2019, by which a sum of ₹30,000 was ordered to be paid to bus passenger on account of his human rights being violated by the crew of the bus. The dispute arose from an incident on January 16, 2016. The complainant, N Ramesh Kumar, alleged that he was travelling on a government bus operating on Route No. 2V when the driver and conductor behaved rudely with him. He claimed that the bus crew forcibly pushed him out of the bus and also failed to issue him a travel ticket. Kumar subsequently approached the SHRC alleging a violation of his human rights. The transport corporation contested the complaint and placed on record documents including the route map and five sheets containing the bus travel records. The SHRC, however, concluded that the route map had been prepared subsequently to defeat the passenger’s claim. On this basis, the Commission held that Kumar’s human rights had been violated and awarded him ₹30,000 as compensation. Before the High Court, Selvan argued that the Commission had failed to properly consider the documents placed before it. He further submitted that the allegations involved a consumer grievance arising from an alleged deficiency in service. Therefore, any remedy available to the passenger lay before the appropriate consumer forum and not the SHRC, the Court was told. The High Court agreed. It noted that the Commission’s findings substantially revolved around the bus journey, issuance of a ticket and the records maintained by the transport corporation. items.title: Banke Bihari Temple: Supreme Court says all donations must go directly to temple treasury
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed that all donations made to the Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan be deposited through the temple’s donation boxes or online, directly into the temple treasury. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Let there be no doubt, and we accordingly direct that every penny of donation must come through the donation boxes or online [into the] temple treasury. Any impediment created by sevayats (temple servants) or anyone else shall be viewed very seriously." Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court also directed the Temple’s managing committee to introduce a transparent mechanism for receiving donations and take all necessary steps to prevent malpractices. The directions were passed in the broader dispute concerning the management and administration of the Banke Bihari Temple, including the manner in which its funds are handled and the constitution of a committee to oversee its affairs. The dispute arose after the Uttar Pradesh government brought the Temple’s management under a statutory framework through the Uttar Pradesh Shri Banke Bihari Ji Temple Trust Ordinance, 2025. The move sought to replace the 1939 Scheme of Management, which has long governed the administration and rituals of the temple, including provisions concerning darshan, religious practices and temple finances. The proposed State-controlled trust had led to questions over the extent of government involvement in the management of religious institutions. In August 2025, the Supreme Court had set up a high-powered committee headed by former Allahabad High Court Justice Ashok Kumar to oversee the temple’s day-to-day functioning. The committee was tasked with ensuring basic amenities for devotees, including drinking water, washrooms, shelters, crowd-management corridors and facilities for vulnerable devotees, besides planning the development of the temple and its surroundings, including land acquisition where necessary. Notably, in May 2025 , the Court had permitted the Uttar Pradesh government to use temple funds to acquire five acres of land around the temple for corridor development, subject to the land being registered in the name of the deity. items.title: Flash floods an 'act of God', ensuing damage to rented building can't be basis of cheating case: J&K High Court
items.summary: Damage caused a building due to flash floods cannot be blamed on its landlord, observed the Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently while quashing a cheating case filed against the landlord and trustees of a school by a person who had taken over its management [ Ghulam Rasool Rather & Ors. v. UT of J&K ]. The woman who had taken over the management claimed that the school's trustees had failed to disclose structural deficiencies in the school building when it was handed over to her. She, therefore, accused the school's trustees and the building's landlord of cheating her. Justice Sanjay Dhar , however, observed that the primary basis for such an allegation was the damage caused to the building after flash floods that occurred in the area in 2013. Flash floods are an act of God and cannot, by itself, form the basis of a criminal cheating case, the Court held. "Merely because water of flash floods entered the school building and it caused damage to the school building does not make out a case of cheating of the petitioners (school trustees, landlord of building). The petitioners/trustees only happen to be the managers of the school and they had transferred the management of the school along with its goodwill to respondent No. 2 (complainant). They had nothing to do with the quality of the school building nor were they responsible for flash floods, which were an act of God," the Court said. Justice Sanjay Dhar The Court reiterated that to constitute the criminal offence of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (now replaced by Section 318 of the BNS, 2023), there must be a fraudulent or dishonest intention. Mere breach of contract or subsequent difficulties cannot automatically give rise to criminal prosecution, it added. The High Court was hearing two petitions to quash a criminal case filed against several trustees of a school, as well as the landlord in whose property the school was being run. The case was registered on a complaint filed in 2021 by a woman to whom the management of the school was transferred in 2012. The complainant alleged that she was assured that the school had a bright future but later discovered several problems relating to the school premises and its management. She said that around 12 inches of water entered the school building during flash floods in November 2013, causing damage and financial losses. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to interfere with Allahabad HC order on demolition of illegal lawyers’ chambers in Lucknow
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to interfere with an Allahabad High Court order directing the demolition of around 72 illegal lawyers’ chambers near the District and Sessions Court in Lucknow [ Central Bar Association v. State of UP & Ors ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta refused a request to refer the dispute to mediation and advised the lawyers occupying the unauthorised structures to vacate them peacefully. It also told the petitioners that the encroachments could not be allowed to continue merely because those occupying them held positions in the local bar association. “Where is this offending construction situated? You tell us. You occupy the main road, you occupy the open space inside the court premises, raise unauthorised construction and then say I am elected as the president of the association, I am member of the governing body and therefore I have a right to continue. No. All demolitions have to take place,” Justice Nath said. Justice Nath added that he had personally witnessed the extent of such encroachments during his time as a judge in the State. “I have seen it myself when I was there for two years as a senior judge. I know what kind of constructions, how the roads have been obstructed, traffic is completely obstructed. Demolition has to take place,” he said. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta Senior Advocate Adish Aggarwala suggested that an alternative location could be allotted to the lawyers. Justice Nath, however, said that the lawyers could approach the State government for assistance in acquiring land rather than occupying public spaces. “You go and purchase some lands for the lawyers over there. Go and request the State government to provide you a society for that,” he said. When counsel sought that the matter be referred to mediation, Justice Nath rejected the suggestion outright. “Mediation with lawyers! No. Dismissed,” he said. Justice Mehta questioned who was responsible for protecting court premises if lawyers themselves were encroaching upon them. “Who is going to protect the court’s precincts? If it is encroached in this manner. Who is responsible? Lawyers don’t have any kind of qualms,” he said. items.title: Supreme Court directs Delhi lawyers bodies to work out women's representation in their governing bodies
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) and bar bodies of the district courts in the national capital to jointly work out a “structured” and “institutionalised” mechanism for representation of women in their governing bodies for the 2027 Bar elections [Fozia Rahman vs. Bar Council of Delhi and Anr.]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed that the Coordination Committee of All District Court Bar Associations of Delhi, in consultation with the DHCBA and other bar bodies, to come out with a proposal reflecting an "all-acceptable solution." The Court granted six weeks for consultations to ensure that any impediments or bottlenecks arising during deliberations are discussed and resolved well in time. The Bench told the DHCBA that the matter was one of its leadership, statesmanship, stewardship and "a question of prestige." The Court also expressed confidence that the coordination committee would arrive at a workable solution. "We have no reason to doubt that the coordination committee will come out with an all-acceptable solution, which shall be a structured, institutionalised representation mechanism, so that repeated orders are not required to be passed by this Court," the Court said in its order. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court passed the order on a petition filed by advocate Fozia Rahman seeking reservation for women lawyers in the DHCBA. On December 19, 2024, the top court had passed interim directions reserving, on an experimental basis, the post of treasurer for women across all Delhi bar associations and one post of designated senior member executive for women in the DHCBA. The Court had also reserved 30 percent of executive committee posts for women in all Delhi district court bar associations on an experimental basis. The Court then had underlined the constitutional mandate for women's representation in governance drawing a parallel with panchayats and other local self-government bodies and held that the same principle should extend to the legal fraternity. items.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court seeks ECI data on appeals pending over voters' exclusion/inclusion
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought detailed data from the Election Commission of India (ECI) on the number of appeals pending before appellate tribunals challenging exclusion/ inclusion of voters from West Bengal's electoral rolls following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing pleas seeking measures to streamline and expedite the disposal of appeals before the SIR appellate tribunals. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court today directed the ECI to provide a break-up of pending and disposed appeals. The information sought includes: 1. items.title: Drivers move Bombay High Court against Marathi language rule, says livelihood of lakhs under threat
items.summary: Four cab drivers, who operate cabs using mobile cab aggregator apps, have moved the Bombay High Court challenging the Maharashtra government’s decision to make working knowledge of Marathi language compulsory for auto rickshaw, taxi and app‑based cab drivers [Mohd. Kasim Ahmad vs. State of Maharashtra]. The petition filed through advocate Vivek Shukla will be mentioned on August 27 before the acting Chief Justice for urgent directions. The rule was notified via a government notification dated August 12. The plea by the cab drivers argues that the Marathi language rule violates their fundamental rights under Articles 14 (right to equality), 19 (freedom to carry on trade and profession) and 21 (right to life) of the Constitution and is ultra vires the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which does not prescribe any language requirement for driving licences. As per the plea, "The parent Act (Motor Vehicles Act) confers no power upon the State Government to prescribe working knowledge of any language as a qualification for a driver, as a condition of a badge, or as a condition of a permit, and confers no power to suspend or revoke a badge on such a ground. The impugned notification manufactures a new disqualification and a new ground of suspension and revocation which the parliament never enacted." Lakhs of poor and migrant drivers face imminent suspension of badges and cancellation of permits, threatening their livelihoods if the rule is implemented, the plea states. The PIL has sought an immediate stay on the government notification so as to prevent hardship to nearly 9.65 lakh drivers across Maharashtra. "The scale of the notification is enormous. As stated by the Hon'ble Transport Minister himself in the press, about 9,65,000 rickshaw and taxi permits and badges have been issued in the State so far. As per the Government's own statements, about 1,65,000 non-Marathi speaking drivers attended the 105 day "Hinduhridaysamrat Balasaheb Thackeray Marathi Language Campaign" conducted through the Konkan Marathi Sahitya Parishad and the Mumbai Marathi Sahitya Sangh. Lakhs of drivers remain exposed to notices, suspension and cancellation," the plea claims.

items.title: Husband can't command wife to do household chores and look after his parents: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently questioned why Indian women are expected to take permission from members of the matrimonial home to visit their own parents' home. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha said that wives cannot be expected to solely do household work. "This Court does not understand why an Indian woman is required to take permission of all present at her matrimonial home to fulfil her basic desire of visiting her parents house as and when she wish and feels to go. This Court is of the view that anyone including husband cannot command and demand any female including his wife to do the household activities and to look after, his parents." The duty of taking care of parents vests upon the son or the daughter and not on the son-in-law or daughter-in-law, the Court added. Reiterating the choice every woman has, the Court said, "A woman has fundamental and absolute right to make decisions concerning her career, finances, etc. Huband cannot compel wife or coerce her to live according to his wishes and expectations. He went on to say she had gone to her parents' house without his permission too many times. The wife alleged that she was assaulted, abused and left injured by the husband and his family. She claimed that she had to tolerate the husband's habits of gambling and alcoholism. Despite the husband now seeking divorce, she was ready to join him. items.title: Karnataka SIR: Age gaps, name mismatches among criteria as 20 lakh voters face notices
items.summary: The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer’s office has listed nine criteria for flagging voters under “anomalies” or “logical discrepancies” during the ongoing SIR. More than 20 lakh electors in Karnataka have been flagged under this category and will receive notices seeking clarification. The criteria relate largely to inconsistencies in the way an elector’s details have been mapped to the previous SIR electoral rolls, including differences in names, unusual age gaps between family members and discrepancies in parent-child relationships. The criteria assume significance, as Karnataka’s draft electoral roll, published on August 24, has 4,46,80,151 electors. Of these, 20,35,835 have been categorised as having anomalies or logical discrepancies, while another 23,45,500 have been placed in the no-mapping category. Together, 43,81,335 electors, or 9.82% of the draft electorate, are set to receive notices. According to the criteria issued by the CEO’s office, an elector can be flagged if the age difference between them and a parent to whom they have been linked is less than 15 years or more than 50 years. A similar anomaly is flagged if the age difference between an elector and three mapped grandparents is less than 40 years. A mismatch in the father’s name between the current electoral roll and the previous SIR roll is also among the criteria. The list also includes cases where two people mapped as children of the same parent have an age gap of less than nine months. Another criterion covers cases where six or more people have been mapped as the children of the same parent, with the system treating this as a possible indication of an incorrect match. An anomaly is also generated where a parent linked to an elector was present in the current electoral roll but was considered invalid, resulting in all progenies mapped to that parent being flagged. The remaining criteria concern discrepancies in an elector’s own name or their father’s name between the current roll and the previous SIR roll. The notices will be handed over by Booth Level Officers and will mention the reason for the notice, the category under which the elector has been flagged, the date and location of the hearing and the documents required for verification. The identification of these criteria comes after questions were raised over the lack of clarity around the “logical discrepancy” category during the SIR process. items.title: New video shows BJP MLA’s daughter slapping woman SI in Karnataka temple
items.summary: Days after a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA’s daughter was booked for assaulting an on-duty police officer, CCTV footage of the altercation between the sub-inspector and the woman at a Mandya temple has surfaced. The incident took place on August 12 at the Arathi Ukkada temple in Srirangapatna taluk during Bhima Amavasya celebrations. Sub-Inspector Savitha B Patil, who is attached to the Mandya Women’s Police Station, had been deployed at the temple for crowd management and security. The woman involved, Aishwarya, is the daughter of Tumakuru Rural BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda and is married to police officer Gautham, an Assistant Commissioner of Police. According to Savitha’s complaint, Aishwarya arrived at the temple and sought to enter the sanctum sanctorum despite the heavy rush. The officer allegedly asked her to wait for a few minutes to avoid inconvenience to other devotees. Aishwarya is then alleged to have questioned why she was being stopped and identified herself as the MLA’s daughter. The argument escalated, with Savitha alleging that Aishwarya verbally abused her, slapped her and threatened to ruin her career. The CCTV footage that has now emerged shows the two women engaged in an argument. Aishwarya is seen using her phone during the exchange before appearing to slap Savitha on the head. The police officer then appears to strike Aishwarya, after which people nearby intervene and separate them. Based on Savitha’s complaint, the Kyathanahalli police registered an FIR against Aishwarya under Sections 132, 115(2), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The charges include allegedly assaulting or using criminal force against a public servant, voluntarily causing hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation. Mandya Superintendent of Police Mallikarjun Baladandi said Aishwarya has also filed a counter-complaint alleging that Savitha abused her. Police are examining the allegations in the counter-complaint. As of Tuesday, no arrest had been reported. MLA Suresh Gowda has apologised for his daughter’s conduct if she is found to have acted improperly and said anyone found guilty should face action under the law. He said Aishwarya had gone to the temple with two young children and had sought permission to enter briefly, as waiting in the queue could have been difficult for them. items.title: Actor Devan to join Vijay’s TVK after quitting BJP, says he was offered Kerala chief post
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Malayalam actor and politician S Devan on Monday, August 24, said he has decided to join Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), the party led by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. Devan recently resigned as the Kerala state vice-president of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He said TVK representatives approached him after his resignation, and that he accepted the invitation following preliminary discussions. A formal announcement about his joining the party is expected after Devan meets Vijay in Chennai on September 10. Devan told the media that TVK had offered him the post of president of its Kerala unit. “I raised certain issues in 2004, and that is exactly what Vijay is raising now. There are certain similarities between Joseph Vijay and me in politics, and that is what attracted me to him,” Devan said. Devan said he entered politics with the aim of fighting corruption and communalism and creating a new political culture. “In 2004, I was the highest-paid villain in south India. I knew that if I entered politics, it would affect my film career. So I made that sacrifice and entered politics,” he said. Devan began his political career during his college days with the Kerala Students Union (KSU), the student wing of the Congress party. He formally entered electoral politics in 2004, when he formed the Kerala People’s Party. He contested the 2004 Wadakkanchery bye-election and the 2006 Assembly election from Thiruvananthapuram on the party’s ticket, but lost both elections. In 2020, Devan renamed and relaunched the party as the Nava Kerala People’s Party. The party merged with the BJP in 2021, following which Devan was appointed vice-president of the BJP's Kerala unit. Devan resigned from the BJP on August 15, announcing his decision at a function at the Kanichukulangara Devi temple in Alappuzha, which is managed by the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam. At the event, Devan said he had felt a lack of “space” and meaningful work during his nearly five years in the BJP. He also accused the BJP’s Kerala unit of moving away from the ideals of social justice espoused by social reformer Sree Narayana Guru.

Around 9.30 pm on Sunday, August 23, Sangeetha got a call from her mother M Kalavathi. “I’ll be late getting home, you have dinner and go to sleep,” she told her. Earlier in the evening, Kalavathi had stepped out of their house in Padi Puthunagar of Chennai’s Anna Nagar West Extension to go to church. Less than two hours later, around 11.20 pm, Sangeetha’s phone rang again. This time, it was the Ayanavaram police calling to ask her to identify the photo of a woman they had found unconscious in a rainwater-filled pit. She had “fainted”, Sangeetha was told. That woman, who was later declared dead at the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital (KMCH), was Kalavathi. Passersby had found the 59-year-old woman unconscious in a pit near the Anna Nagar Tower Metro station in Chennai and alerted the police. With the help of the public, they pulled her out and took her to KMCH, where doctors declared her brought dead. The police told the family that when onlookers tried to lift her out of the pit, they had experienced minor electric shocks, raising suspicion that Kalavathi had been electrocuted after falling into the pit. “The Thirumangalam police said she had slipped into the pit and got electrocuted. When they tried to lift her, they said they felt an electric shock,” Sangeetha told TNM. Kalavathi, who worked as a housekeeping employee at a sweet shop in Anna Nagar, lived with her daughter Sangeetha, 28. Her body was sent to the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital mortuary for post-mortem examination. The K4 Anna Nagar Police have registered a case under Section 194 (unnatural or suspicious deaths) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The exact cause of death can be established only after the report of the post-mortem examination is received. ‘Negligence of authorities killed Kalavathi’ The family alleged that it is the negligence of the civic authorities that is behind Kalavathi’s death, as they had failed to barricade the pit or put up warnings for pedestrians. Reports suggest that the pit she fell into had been dug as part of the construction of a stormwater drain. Meanwhile, Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) officials have denied that there was an open trench at the spot. There is a height difference between the footpath and the road, which was waterlogged after rains, according to GCC officials. items.title: Kerala: Temple worker alleges suspension after daughter marries outside caste
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A temple worker in Kannur has alleged that he was suspended from his duties after his daughter married a man from another caste. CV Rajan, a 58-year-old resident of Karivellur, who has worked as an upakarmi (temple assistant) at the Karivelloor Muchilot Bhagavathi Temple for three decades, has approached the Malabar Devaswom Board with a complaint against the suspension. The allegation, meanwhile, has been disputed by the temple authorities, who have cited alleged violations of temple practices and misconduct as the reasons for the action. Rajan's family has been associated with the temple for generations, and he took up the job after his father. He told TNM he has not been working at the temple for about four months now. He was initially suspended in March and asked to explain the allegations against him by April 1. The temple later issued a formal suspension order effective June 15, stating that his explanation was unsatisfactory. Rajan’s daughter married a man from the Pothuval community on March 15. Rajan belongs to the Vaniya community, which is classified as an Other Backward Class (OBC) in Kerala, while Pothuval is classified under the general category, according to the state’s classification. The temple Rajan worked at is dedicated to Muchilot Bhagavathy, the chief deity associated with the Vaniya community. Rajan said the issue was discussed at the temple’s general body meeting in 2025, around the time of his daughter’s engagement, and that it was decided that he could continue working at the temple. “During the engagement time of my daughter, the temple general body discussed this matter and decided that I could continue my job. Later, in 2026, the new executive committee and trustee asked me to stay away from the job without initially giving any formal letter," he said. According to Rajan, the temple’s trust and executive committee orally asked him to stay away from his duties three days before his daughter’s wedding.
